messages:
maria_support: @here Customer (Acme Media / jordan) opened an escalation — intermittent 502/504s from Hosted Inference started ~2026-03-14 22:10 UTC, spike during heavy batch runs. They report SDK retry loops and a billing surprise. Attaching quick summary and repro steps below.

maria_support: Symptoms: ~2–5% of requests returning 502 or 504, mostly during sustained high concurrency (80–150 concurrent streams). SDK shows repeated retries (attempt=3) and then client-level timeout. Customer says some of the retried calls were billed twice.

customer_jordan: seeing this across eu-west-1 and us-west-2, same model (gpt-open-13b), using streaming for tokens. We hit it with a player-encoding job (avg tokens 1800 per request). SDK version: 2.4.1. Node.

maria_support: Repro steps (shared by customer):
1) Node script (parallel 120 workers), each does streaming generate for ~1800 tokens.
2) Run for 5 minutes. Failure rate rises after ~45s.
3) When failures occur, SDK logs show backoff/retry loops; example lines below.

maria_support: SDK log excerpt:
```
[2026-03-14T22:12:03Z] request_id=rid_02ab attempt=1 status=200
[2026-03-14T22:12:09Z] request_id=rid_02ab attempt=2 error=EPIPE write after end
[2026-03-14T22:12:09Z] request_id=rid_02ab attempt=3 status=502 upstream_bad_gateway
[2026-03-14T22:12:10Z] request_id=rid_02ab fatal=client_timeout
```

maria_support: Curl repro (non-streaming) customer tried:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example/v1/generate \
  -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-open-13b","input":"<long prompt>","max_tokens":1800}'
```

sam_infra: assigning myself to check LB/gateway connection pools and upstream health. Can you paste the exact region and approximate QPS you saw? Also whether they used keepalive on their client or ephemeral connections?

maria_support: QPS ~70–90 sustained, spikes to 120. They use default Node SDK keepalive (no explicit agent). Region: eu-west-1 and us-west-2.

alex_runtime: from the runtime side: 502 + EPIPE could be TLS socket resets or upstream worker oom/evict. 504 suggests gateway timeout while waiting on a backend. Two parallel possibilities: (1) connection churn + head-of-line blocking under streaming leads to closed sockets mid-stream, (2) SDK retry concurrency opens more simultaneous connections causing transient overload on a gateway pool.

alex_runtime: quick ask: can we get a sample request_id from a failing call, so we can grep gateway logs? customer_jordan, any request_id you can share?

customer_jordan: provided rid_02ab and rid_02c4 in DM. Also saw repeated request ids in billing export around spike window.

sam_infra: pulled gateway logs for rid_02ab across both regions. Observed: rapid sequence of TCP connection reuses followed by `upstream prematurely closed connection while reading response header` from the uproxy. Snapshot log lines:
```
2026-03-14T22:12:09Z rid=rid_02ab upstream=worker-13 status=502 msg="upstream prematurely closed"
2026-03-14T22:12:09Z rid=rid_02ab conn=pool-17 in_flight=7
```

sam_infra: notes: in_flight=7 on that upstream at the moment — we saw several upstreams hit 6–8 concurrent streams. Our configured per-worker connection limit is 8 for streaming workloads. If incoming concurrency pushes that, new requests get routed to overloaded upstreams which may abort streaming responses.

alex_runtime: aha — that's consistent. When an upstream aborts mid-stream, the client may retry. If retry lands on another worker, fine, but if the initial worker had partially succeeded and billing counted the accepted tokens before abort (or the billing event was emitted at accept), customer could see double charges.

leah_billing: looping in billing. We need the list of request ids and timestamps to verify duplicate billing events. If we confirm duplicates we'll credit. Also want to know whether SDK retries used idempotency keys.

maria_support: customer says they did not set idempotency keys in their calls (default SDK usage).

leah_billing: OK. Billing team will reconcile for the window 2026-03-14T22:10:00–22:20:00 UTC. Please collect request_ids (they already shared a subset).

alex_runtime: mitigation path: 1) reduce per-client concurrency or enable HTTP keepalive agent with connection pooling so a single connection is reused rather than opening many ephemeral connections; 2) for immediate relief, disable streaming on hotspot job or reduce batch size (less long-lived streams); 3) we can also temporarily increase per-worker connection limit, but that risks OOM if too many streams held in memory.

maria_support: Customer tried disabling streaming — reported fewer errors. So that aligns. They're asking for a long-term fix and whether we should change server-side connection limits or introduce tokenization of retries.

sam_infra: short-term we've applied a soft throttle at the gateway for that customer to keep per-backend in_flight under 6. This reduces 502s but increases queueing latency slightly. Deployed at 22:45 UTC to eu-west-1.

ops-bot: deploy:gateway-throttle/customer-acme applied by sam_infra at 2026-03-14T22:45:32Z :white_check_mark:

customer_jordan: after throttle — error rate dropped from ~4% to ~0.6% in eu-west-1, thanks. Still seeing occasional 504s in us-west-2.

alex_runtime: for us-west-2 we'll also bump the per-worker connection limit from 8->12 for a canary subset of workers (10% of pool) to observe memory/latency impact. Sam — can you schedule that canary?

sam_infra: starting canary now for us-west-2 group-05. Will monitor memory and p95 latency for 30m.

leah_billing: billing update: we matched ~11 request_ids that appear twice in usage events in the window. We'll issue credits and follow up with txn ids. Will also work with runtime to ensure billing emission point is aligned to final completion (avoid counting before final status) — this is a separate change request.

alex_runtime: action items:
- (alex) instrument gateway to emit a final completion event downstream only after stream finalization (avoid double-count on mid-stream abort).
- (sam) monitor canary for us-west-2 and report.
- (leah) confirm credit flow and customer-facing billing note.
- (maria) coordinate customer comms and share interim mitigation (throttle + disable streaming if possible).

maria_support: customer update posted: "we applied a temporary throttle and recommend you try disabling streaming or reducing concurrency. We're also investigating and will credit any duplicate charges." They asked for ETA on the runtime fix.

alex_runtime: ETA: I'll have a small change to gate billing emit (move to post-finalize hook) and a rollout plan — aiming for staging deploy tomorrow 03/15 and prod 03/17 pending validation. Estimate 48–72h.

sam_infra: canary results: after 25m, memory p95 increase +4%, no OOMs, p95 latency +10ms. Error rate in canary group dropped to ~0.3%. I'll expand to 30% if stable.

customer_jordan: thanks — we'll keep streams off for now and reduce parallelism. Appreciate the quick response.

maria_support: leaving thread open for the runtime billing fix and final credits. Please post follow-ups here.

alex_runtime: will post a deployment PR and a short postmortem summarizing root cause and the billing emission change once implemented."
